title: Navier-Stokes Fluid Dynamics Modeling of Leaf Boundary Layer Thermal Transport under Micro-Vectored Airflow
author: Dr. vmffkxhs2362
abstract: Stagnant boundary layers ($r_b > 250\text{ s/m}$) restrict $CO_2$ diffusion and transpirational cooling in dense vertical farm canopies. We solved 3D Navier-Stokes equations coupled with heat and mass transfer models under micro-vectored vertical air velocities ranging from 0.05 to 0.6 m/s. Maintaining canopy velocity at 0.35 m/s reduced boundary layer resistance to 42 s/m, elevating net photosynthetic rate ($P_n$) by 26.4%.
key_findings: Micro-vectored airflow at 0.35 m/s thinned boundary layer thickness from 3.2 mm down to 0.6 mm.
Transpirational calcium flux to apical meristems increased by 44.1%, eliminating tip-burn necrosis.
$CO_2$ assimilation rate ($P_n$) stabilized at 22.8 μmol $CO_2$/m²/s under 1000 ppm ambient $CO_2$.
